in_arabic.name: ممججد
in_arabic.meaning: منعم و بزرگراہنده، مجد و جلال بخشنده
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم مُمَجِّد از ریشه 'مجد' است که دلالت بر عظمت و بزرگی دارد. این نام یکی از اسماء الله است و به معنای منعم و بزرگراهنده، مجد و جلال بخشنده است. در قرآن کریم نیز به این معنی اشاره شده است.

in_urdu.name: ممججد
in_urdu.meaning: منعم و بزرگراہنده، مجد و جلال بخشنده
in_urdu.long_meaning: ممججد کا نام عربی زبان کی روٹ 'مجد' سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے عظمت اور بزرگی۔ یہ نام اللہ کے ناموں میں سے ایک ہے اور اس کا مطلب ہے منعم و بزرگراہنده، مجد و جلال بخشنده۔ جنوبی ایشیائی مسلم روایت میں اس کا خاص اہمیت ہے۔

in_hindi.name: मुमज्जिद
in_hindi.meaning: मुमज्जिद का अर्थ है महानता और समृद्धि प्रदान करने वाला
in_hindi.long_meaning: मुमज्जिद नाम अरबी भाषा की जड़ 'मजद' से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है महानता और समृद्धि। यह नाम अल्लाह के नामों में से एक है और इसका अर्थ है महानता और समृद्धि प्रदान करने वाला। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में इस नाम का विशेष महत्व है।

in_pashto.name: ممججد
in_pashto.meaning: د مجد او ل greatnessفور وړاندی، د عظمت ورکړی
in_pashto.long_meaning: ممججد نوم د عربي ژبې د ريښې 'مجد' څخه اخیستل شوی دی، چې معنی یې د عظمت او ل greatnessفور دی. دا نوم د الله نومونو څخه يو دی او د مجد او جلال ورکړی، د greatnessفور او عظمت بخشي معنی لري. په افغان او پښتني روايت کې دا نوم خاص اهميت لري.

in_english.name: Mumajjid
in_english.meaning: glorifier, bestower of greatness and honor
in_english.long_meaning: The name Mumajjid is derived from the Arabic root 'majd', which signifies glory, greatness, and honor. As one of the Names of Allah, Mumajjid means the glorifier, bestower of greatness and honor. It holds significant spiritual and cultural importance in Islamic tradition, reflecting attributes of divine generosity and elevation.

data.cultural_impact: The name Mumajjid evokes a powerful image of courage and dedication to one's faith. Throughout Islamic history, Mumajjids have played essential roles in defending Muslim communities against external threats, spread the message of Islam, and established Islamic states or caliphates. The figure of a Mumajjid embodies the virtues of self-sacrifice, bravery, resilience, and unwavering faith in Allah.
data.spiritual_significance: On a more profound level, the name Mumajjid signifies a warrior in the spiritual battle against inner desires that lead away from Allah. Every believer is called to be a Mumajjid in their own life, defending their faith through the personal struggle of maintaining a strong bond with Allah, upholding moral values, and practicing compassion. The name serves as a constant reminder of the importance of staying true to one's faith in a world with numerous distractions, temptations, and challenges. Embracing the label of a Mumajjid signifies a commitment to the pursuit of Allah's pleasure and striving to create a faithful, supportive community.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Hajar al-Haytami (d. 1566 CE): In his book 'Al-Fatawa al-Hadithiyya', he mentions a man named Mumajjid ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab, who was a contemporary of Ibn Taymiyya (d. 1328 CE). He was a scholar from the Najd region and a supporter of Ibn Taymiyya's teachings. He was also known for his fervor and zeal in spreading the faith.
historical_references.context: Ibn Hajar al-Haytami's reference to Mumajjid ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab as a contemporary of Ibn Taymiyya and a supporter of his teachings places him in the 13th-14th centuries CE. Mumajjid was known for his zeal and fervor in spreading the faith.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Kathir (d. 1373 CE): In his historical work 'Al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya', he mentions Mumajjid ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab as a scholar from the Najd region who led a military expedition against the Yemeni city of San'a in 1257 CE. He was known for his piety and his opposition to the Shia and the Mongols.
